questions.text: What is the basic purpose of an adhesive in BCI?

options.text: To secure the surfaces of two materials together
To replace all mechanical fasteners in structural work
To waterproof every joint regardless of substrate
To provide only a decorative surface coating

questions.rationale: BCI defines adhesives as materials used to secure the surfaces of two materials together.
questions.explanation: Compatibility is poor; adhesion will fail within weeks. Primer does not solve the incompatibility; substrate preparation (removal of old sealant) is required. No chemical bond occurs; mechanical adhesion is impossible. Silicone and acrylic are chemically incompatible. Silicone has very low surface energy and does not wet acrylic. Complete removal of old sealant to bare substrate is mandatory. When changing sealant types, remove old sealant completely. Never assume chemical compatibility.
questions.code_citation: ASTM C920 Substrate Preparation and Sealant Compatibility Guidelines

questions.text: Which adhesive selection factor asks how the bond resists loads?
questions.rationale: BCI lists strength as an important adhesive selection factor.
questions.explanation: Pressure-sensitive adhesives are for temporary bonding (tapes, labels). Polyurethane adhesives are more flexible; preferred for wood-to-wood applications. Silicone adhesives are flexible and not suitable for structural concrete bonding. Epoxy adhesives are two-part, high-strength products specifically designed for rigid bonding of concrete and metal. They develop full strength after 24-48 hours. Epoxy = structural bonding (concrete, metal); Polyurethane = wood-to-wood or movement-accommodating applications.

questions.text: According to BCI, adhesives are usually strongest against which stresses?
questions.rationale: BCI states adhesives are usually strongest in tensile and shear stresses.
questions.explanation: Acrylic is water-based and sensitive to rain during cure; it requires 24-48 dry hours. Butyl sealants are non-hardening; they do not cure. Polysulfide sealants are moisture-tolerant but require longer cure times than polyurethane. Polyurethane sealants are moisture-curing; water triggers the cure reaction, allowing application in humid conditions or during light rain. Polyurethane = moisture-curing; ideal for tropical and humid climates.

questions.text: According to BCI, adhesives are usually weakest against which stresses?
questions.rationale: BCI identifies cleavage or splitting stresses as the weaker stress condition for adhesives.

questions.text: Which common adhesive does BCI describe as quick-setting, non-staining, and slightly resilient?
questions.rationale: BCI describes white or polyvinyl glue as setting quickly, not staining, and being slightly resilient.
questions.code_citation: Tropical climate engineering practice and product data sheets

questions.text: Which adhesive type does BCI describe as extremely strong and usable on porous and nonporous materials?
questions.rationale: BCI states epoxy resins are extremely strong and may secure both porous and nonporous materials.
questions.explanation: The comparison is reversed; sealants are flexible. Both types are used for multiple substrates; application determines the choice. The terms are not interchangeable; they serve different functions. Adhesives bond substrates rigidly; sealants remain elastic to accommodate joint movement and prevent air/water infiltration. This is the fundamental distinction. Adhesive = permanent rigid bond. Sealant = flexible, accommodates movement.
questions.code_citation: ASTM C920 Sealant Standard and ASTM D2382 Adhesive Standard

questions.text: A large plastic laminate sheet must be bonded without clamping. Which BCI adhesive family matches this cue?

options.text: Animal glue for stable indoor heat and humidity
A sealer used only to fill surface pores
A backup material for caulking depth control

questions.rationale: BCI states contact cement bonds on contact, generally does not require clamping, and is used for large sheet materials such as plastic laminate.
questions.code_citation: ASTM C920 Sealant Product Data and Durability Standards

questions.text: Which adhesive does BCI associate with large sheet materials such as plastic laminate?
questions.rationale: BCI gives plastic laminate as an example use for contact cement.

questions.text: In Salvan, what does adhesiveness mean?

options.text: The ability of a material to cling to a different material
The ability of one material to keep its own particles together
The ability of a surface to become glossy
The ability of a wall to carry vertical load

questions.rationale: Salvan distinguishes adhesiveness as clinging to a different material.

questions.text: What is the purpose of sealing compounds in Salvan?

options.text: To fill surface pores and form a continuous skin against liquid movement
To calculate the volume of lumber
To set the number of hollow blocks per square meter

questions.rationale: Salvan describes sealing compounds as filling pores and forming a continuous skin against liquid penetration or escape.
